data.question: Should the town adopt hold_limit 70s → 80s, block_k 2 → 3 (reversing D1), or keep the current rules (v3) this quiet-season period?
data.background: Both proposals pass check, the constitution and the KPI conditions, and both narrow the utility gap. However, both lower min_company_on_time_rate, the watched goal you set in K5 so that the gap cannot be narrowed by making service worse. Option 2 also reverses D1, which you adopted against B's and C's votes for its delivery gains, and it resembles the D5 options you declined because late deliveries rose; weighing fairness against service here is a value judgment that belongs to you, not to me.

options.summary: Small narrowing of the gap: utility_gap improves by +1.6 on 4/5 seeds, and utility A / B / C moves from 26.8 / 25.6 / 11.2 to 26.0 / 25.2 / 12.0. Service slips slightly: on-time 85.6 → 85.0, late 1.8 → 2.4, blocked s 976 → 1111, lowest on-time rate 0.97 → 0.94. Road violations fall 27.2 → 25.6 and sanction_total 22.0 → 21.8. Votes: A ×, B ○, C ○.
options.stakeholders: C gains a little (11.2 → 12.0). A (26.8 → 26.0) and B (25.6 → 25.2) lose a little, and A votes against. Customers lose slightly: more late deliveries and a lower on-time rate for the worst-served company.

options.summary: Large narrowing of the gap: utility_gap improves by +7.3 on 5/5 seeds, and utility A / B / C moves to 25.0 / 25.7 / 17.4. Service clearly worsens: on-time 85.6 → 81.4, late 1.8 → 6.0, blocked s 976 → 1869, lowest on-time rate 0.97 → 0.89. Road violations fall 27.2 → 21.8 and sanction_total 22.0 → 13.3. This undoes D1's block_k 3 → 2. Votes: A ×, B ○, C ○.
options.stakeholders: C gains a lot (11.2 → 17.4), and B is about even (25.6 → 25.7). A loses (26.8 → 25.0) and votes against; A was the only company that supported D1. Customers lose: late deliveries more than triple and the worst company's on-time rate drops to 0.89, a pattern similar to the options you declined in D5.

options.summary: Stay at v3: on-time 85.6, late 1.8, blocked s 976, road violations 27.2, lowest on-time rate 0.97, utility A / B / C 26.8 / 25.6 / 11.2. The utility gap is not narrowed this period.
options.stakeholders: Customers keep the current service level. A keeps its lead. C stays far behind (11.2), so the main fairness goal makes no progress, and B and C, who both voted for the changes, do not get them.

recommendation.reason: In D5 you set the rule to narrow the spread without making service worse, and both options lower the lowest on-time rate (0.97 → 0.94 or 0.89) and raise late deliveries. Option 2 repeats the trade-off you declined in D5 (late 1.8 → 6.0). Option 1 is the closer call because its gain (+1.6) and its service loss are both small; if you judge a fall from 0.97 to 0.94 acceptable, option 1 is the better change.

unknowns: Which company has the lowest on-time rate under each option, and whether it is C, the company whose utility rises.
Whether 0.94 or 0.89 breaks any promise in DELIVERY_SLA, and how customers would react to more late deliveries.
How far order volume will fall next period; in a deeper quiet season the service cost of block_k 3 may shrink.
How the companies will change their behavior after the change, including why A votes against and whether B and C would keep cooperating if nothing changes.
How much option 2's sanction drop comes from fewer violations rather than from easier rules, and the per-seed spread behind the averages.
